chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by late polemical/application rhetoric against monotheism and by Christian/Gospel proof-texting (two-trees / five-trees, beloved son, holy spirit, last-day advent). The only recoverable substrate fragment is the bare cosmological axiom of the two primordial Essences (Light and Darkness), embedded inside a hagiographic vision-frame in ¶1. Strong editorial fatigue is visible: the second half concentrates exhortation and judgement language.

paragraphs.core_text: the] two essences that are present at the beginning [ ... ] the Light and the Darkness, that which is good and that which is evi[], life and] death.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed hagiographic vision-frame and speaker attribution: "Once again, when our father looked, he saw a [ ... ] person [ ... ] before him. [He] says [ ... the]" — late frame wrapping a basic dualist axiom.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core fragment is a compact, system-internal cosmological claim (two primordial Essences: Light/Darkness). The surrounding visionary scene and narration (“Once again… our father… he saw… before him”) are compilation frame markers.
Direct audience address and polemical setup against contemporaries who claim “a single essence”; cosmos→contemporary doctrinal dispute (application voice), not systematic cosmological exposition.

Rhetorical catalogue of human vices and social-religious practices (idols, adultery, Mammon, sorceries). This is cosmos→world moral/polemical argumentation rather than system-internal correspondential mapping.
Imperatival polemic (“why do you annul… If they are his, you do them!”) and disciplinary/judgement rhetoric; not cosmological mechanism.

Christianizing argumentative overlay: “beloved son”, “apostles”, and clear dependence on the Gospel ‘tree/fruit’ proof-text (“bitter trees that give not fruit”). Even where it gestures to dualism, the entry-vector is NT-style proof.
Explicit citation style (“Once again he says”) plus father/son/holy spirit and the ‘five trees’ development of the good/evil trees proof-text: Gospel-derived overlay material.
Eschatological condemnation at “the last day” and “his advent” in the presence of God/“beloved son”/“holy spirit” — Christian eschatological register characteristic of later overlay.
Application/exhortation to the hearers about post-mortem verification and impartial judgement; lacks system-internal cosmological mapping and functions as a closing warning (pastoral application).
